quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. This helps the vehicle roll off the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The highway ahead curves only to the right.
The highway ahead turns sharply to the right.
The highway ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
The highway ahead curves to the left and then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ____ light will soon appear.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign shows that traffic must flow only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on country roads is:
questions.explanation: The speed limit on country roads is 55 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it difficult for you to see clearly, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.

questions.explanation: In poor weather or darkness, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will exit the freeway. You can either change lanes to stay on the freeway or stay in your lane and exit.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look through the rear window. Mirrors do not show everything behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, driving away from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder when changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for:

options.text: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you have a clear view of the road.

questions.question: You have enough space to return to the driving lane after passing another car when:

options.text: The other driver signals you to re-enter the lane.
You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to the driving lane after passing, make sure there is safe distance between your car and the passed car. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the lane.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires can push water away. When you go faster than 35 mph, tires cannot move the water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because another vehicle is unlikely to be coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line next to it and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving onto the highway shoulder. Do not pass by crossing a solid yellow line.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when needed to avoid a crash. Do not use your horn at slow drivers or to tell them to move out of your way.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop than it would on normal roads.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic and do not follow other cars too closely. Watch carefully for workers and machines in the zone.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams will reflect back to you and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents, fires, or other disasters just to look.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, be ready for changes in traffic. Watch for signals from other drivers. Expect cars entering at on-ramps and be ready for quick changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Over your left or right shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot when changing lanes.
